markets_mock.dart has:

- ETH `changePct: -0.4,` and `third: '−0.004%'`, with `'Funding': -0.004`
- SOL `changePct: 3.8,` and `'Funding': 0.012`

trade_mock.dart:93 and :101 agree with Markets (`changePct: -0.4,` and `changePct: 3.8,`). The card renders `change: b.change` (arena_screen.dart:134), so ETH shows `− 0.8%` while Markets shows −0.4%.

The Funding sort is currently pinned on a tie. home_screen_test.dart:957-958 reads `// ETH and SOL pay the same funding: the tie goes by id.` then `expect(tickers(tester), ['ETH', 'SOL', 'BTC']);`. With Markets values the order becomes SOL 0.012, BTC 0.009, ETH -0.004, so ETH moves from first to last. Change stays ['SOL','BTC','ETH'] (3.8 > 1.2 > -0.4).

Volume needs no change. Markets has no volume column; its Volume chip orders by OI (412/290/180), and Arena volume (184e9 / 92e9 / 41e9 cents) gives the same BTC > ETH > SOL order.

The ETH bear thesis says `'Funding is hot at 0.03% and spot is not following the perps.'` (lines 153 and 176), which contradicts −0.004%. No test references that string (grep of app/test).

Once aligned, the live fixtures have no tie on any key. Spec 04 still requires 'stable tiebreak by id', and house rule 11 wants that test on a test-local fixture. visible() currently reads only the static `battles` (`for (final b in battles)` in asked()), so it needs an optional pool parameter defaulting to `battles`.

Why fields and not lookups: I chose to align the literals and add a guard test instead of making changePct/fundingPct read MarketsMock. Lookups would remove the constructor fields, and then a test-local fixture could not carry its own values to exercise Change versus Funding. The guard test gives the same protection against drift.

Caveat for the writer: with Markets values, Change and Funding produce the same live order (SOL, BTC, ETH). The widget test therefore cannot tell those two keys apart, and the unit test below is what does.

verdicts.evidence:
The claim holds against the tree.

arena_screen.dart:105-107 builds the list as `child: ListView(` / `keyboardDismissBehavior: ScrollViewKeyboardDismissBehavior.onDrag,` / `padding: ...`, with no controller and no key. The ListenableBuilder rebuilds the same ListView in place when Scenario.arena changes (arena_screen.dart:61-68), so the ScrollPosition survives and clamps to the new maxScrollExtent.

The range path is `onChanged: (v) => Scenario.setArena(from: (v.start * _n).round(), to: (v.end * _n).round(),)` (crowd_filter_panel.dart:60-63). Ask goes through `onChanged: (q) => Scenario.setArena(query: q)` (arena_screen.dart:57). Both set the `ValueNotifier<ArenaView>` at scenario.dart:76.

The review's probe recorded `PROBE 360x640@1.0 ... offset=135.0` after `drag(list, -4000)` then `Scenario.setArena(from: 7, to: 8)`. This is consistent with no controller existing to reset the offset.

Fix per house rule 12: own a ScrollController, and in the existing Scenario.arena listener (renamed from _followQuery to _followView) jump to 0 when the visible count drops.

The listener runs outside build, from a gesture or text callback, so jumpTo there is safe. Sort changes keep the count and so never jump. Reset only grows the set and so never jumps.

The empty-state test only empties the list from the upper thumb, so it can't tell Show all from resetting only the upper bound.

app/lib/features/arena/arena_screen.dart:174-175 has `onPressed: () => Scenario.setArena(from: 0, to: ArenaMock.bucketCount),`, and scenario.dart:99-106 setArena keeps any bound passed as null (`from: from ?? v.from`).

The test (home_screen_test.dart:993) uses `dragThumb(tester, 1, 0.2)`, which gives from=0, to=2, with buckets BTC 2, ETH 4, SOL 7 per `(max(bullPct,100-bullPct)-50) ~/ 5`. So a mutant that sets only `to:` leaves from=0 and still yields '50/50 +' and '3 battles'. mutate.py's show-all-noop drops both bounds, not one.

The lower-thumb empty state is reachable in the app. VistaRangeSlider (vista_market.dart) allows a one-bucket width: `if (v.end - v.start >= 1 / divisions - 1e-9) onChanged(v);`.
